pl-l4d47c2-d1e115.summary: States that not Christ alone will judge, but the saints with him will judge the nations; he told the apostles, you will sit on twelve thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel.
claims: The saints will judge with Christ.

pl-l4d47c2-d1e124.summary: Argues that this was not promised only to the twelve: where will Paul sit, who labored more than all, if only twelve sit?
claims: The promise extends beyond the twelve.

pl-l4d47c2-d1e127.summary: Explains that the twelve thrones signify the perfection of the tribunal, the totality of judges, all the perfect who left all and followed Christ; the twelve tribes signify the totality of those to be judged.
claims: Twelve thrones signify all the perfect.

pl-l4d47c2-d1e143.summary: States that the saints will judge not only by comparison but by authority and power, as the two-edged swords in their hands signify the sentence on good and bad in their power.

pl-l4d47c2-d1e149.summary: Holds that what their power or authority in judging is cannot be known before it is seen, unless by divine revelation.
claims: The saints' judicial power is unknown before it is seen.

pl-l4d47c2.summary: Not Christ alone will judge, but the saints with him, as he promised the apostles twelve thrones; not only the twelve, since Paul, who labored most, must also sit; the twelve thrones signify the perfection of the tribunal, all the perfect who left all and followed Christ, and the twelve tribes all who are judged. The saints will judge not only by comparison but by authority and power, holding the two-edged sword of sentence; what that power is cannot be known before it is seen, except by revelation.
claims: The saints will judge with Christ.
The twelve thrones signify all the perfect.
The saints judge by authority, not only comparison.
The nature of their power is unknown before it is seen.
